title: Humans of Kashi | Faces & Stories
subtext: My first experience photographing strangers on the streets of Kashi, capturing faces, emotions and stories along the way.
content:
They say the best way to know a place is through its people. Being solo, in the beginning I didn’t really have the courage to talk to anyone. Forget the babas, not even the friendly kids who spend most of their time on the ghats. Not because they weren’t welcoming, but because I think I still had to get rid of something within myself.


At first, conversations were just an excuse for a portrait, nothing more. Then they became longer. About life, routines, this place, and its people. Small moments followed. Sharing evening tea just to sit longer (even though I don’t drink tea). Helping kids sell their last stock of flowers. Noticing the same faces and their daily rituals on the ghats.

Once you move beyond the transactional conversations, it becomes easy to notice a quiet contentment in the way people look at life here. And, somewhere along the way, what would have been mere portraits turned into human stories that will stay with me.
